title: How to Turn JPG Images into a PDF
description: Combine JPG photos or scans into a PDF, order pages, choose page layout and review the resulting document before sending it.
intro: Putting images into a PDF makes a group of photos or scans easier to distribute as one document. Good preparation helps keep the pages in order, readable and appropriately sized.

sections.heading: Prepare and order the images
paragraphs: Choose the image files you intend to include and put them in reading order. Clear filenames can help, but check the order in the tool before creating the PDF.
Rotate sideways photos and crop distracting borders first if needed. Avoid enlarging low-resolution images, since a PDF cannot recreate missing detail.

sections.heading: Choose the page layout
paragraphs: A fit-to-image page can preserve each image's proportions, while a standard paper size can make a document easier to print. Orientation and margins affect how the image sits on the page.
If printing matters, check that content is not too close to page edges and that the output dimensions match the recipient's needs.

sections.heading: Create and inspect the PDF
paragraphs: Open JPG to PDF, select your images, configure page size, orientation and margins, then create the document. Check page count, order, cropping and image clarity before sharing.
For a smaller PDF, compress a copy after reviewing the original output. If you need to extract the pages back out later, use PDF to JPG.

faq.question: Can I put multiple JPGs in one PDF?
faq.answer: Yes. Select multiple images and arrange their order before generating the PDF.

faq.question: Will the PDF improve image quality?
faq.answer: No. It places the existing image pixels on a page; it cannot restore detail absent from the source image.

faq.question: Can each image use a different orientation?
faq.answer: Some workflows support per-image settings; otherwise choose a layout that suits the set and review each page in the finished PDF.

faq.question: Are the source JPGs changed?
faq.answer: The tool creates a separate PDF output. Keep your originals as a backup.
